articles.title: Swansea braced to lose Vítor Matos as Strasbourg seek to replace Hugo Oliveira
articles.summary: Matos has indicated a desire for move to Ligue 1. Championship club would be due compensation. Swansea City are increasingly resigned to their head coach, Vítor Matos, joining Strasbourg after he indicated a desire to join Chelsea’s sister club.
body: Strasbourg, acquired by Chelsea’s parent company BlueCo in 2023, have identified Matos as a replacement for Oliveira, who has won three of 10 league matches since succeeding Gary O’Neil in July. The French club are hovering two points above the relegation zone.
Matos is under contract until 2030 and Swansea would be due significant compensation for the 38-year-old, a former Liverpool academy and development team coach.

Matos has won admirers since taking charge of Swansea last November and, despite one win in their past five games, has the south Wales club in the Championship playoff spots. Swansea finished last season in 11th and backed Matos in the transfer market this summer in the hope of pushing on.
Swansea’s next match is at home to West Brom on Saturday, before a trip to Middlesbrough and a south Wales derby against Cardiff in the Welsh capital.

articles.title: Police raid fails to locate three stolen Melbourne Cup trophies worth $1m each
articles.summary: Officers searched a Mount Waverley home in Melbourne after trophies belonging to winning horse Makybe Diva were stolen from Flemington racecourse. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: A police raid has failed to locate three Melbourne Cup trophies belonging to champion horse Makybe Diva after a smash and grab at Flemington racecourse.
A Mount Waverley home in Melbourne’s east was raided on Monday evening after thieves smashed their way into a glass display case at the racecourse about 6.30am.
A 36-year-old Malvern East man was arrested at the Solomon Street home.
The trophies, which Victoria police says are valued at $1m each, are yet to be recovered.

articles.title: 'Is that not match-fixing?' - Erasmus questions officiating
articles.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus predicts Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will not face a ban after being cited, and questions standards in officiating.
body: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has predicted Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast will not face a ban after being cited, and questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?"
Prendergast became the first player to be cited under World Rugby's new regulations for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji and could be banned for Saturday's Nations Championship match.

Speaking at a media conference on Monday, Erasmus said the 23-year-old's tackle was "terrible", but he believes Prendergast will be free to play against the Springboks in Dublin because of a "technicality".

The 54-year-old also added that he thought it was an "immediate red card" when he saw the tackle occur in the first half of Ireland's 43-15 win, but it was not penalised in-game by referee Angus Gardner or by the television match official Mike Adamson.

articles.title: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
articles.summary: As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America. Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past.
body: So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.
“You know what I noticed?” Pochettino asked, smiling as he recounted the story during a meeting with reporters on Monday. “[Guardiola had a] good relationship with JT.”

Back then, Pochettino didn’t seem to be going anywhere. Only a month earlier, he’d signed a four-year contract to guide the US through the 2030 World Cup. Guardiola was, and still is, in the middle of a year-long sabbatical from coaching. He remains the federation’s white whale, often mentioned in the same breath as the US job over the past decade-plus but just as quickly dismissed as a pipe dream.

Just three months after taking in that game at Yankee Stadium, Pochettino is on his way to Manchester United and Guardiola has once again found himself at the center of the rumor mill, with reports suggesting that he and US Soccer are set for exploratory talks.

articles.title: Nations League: Wirtz doubles up as Germany rout Netherlands to top group
articles.summary: Jürgen Klopp’s side make statement with 5-0 triumph. Dutch advance, Greece miss out despite win over Serbia. Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany delivered a 5-0 rout of the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday, reaching the Nations League quarter-finals as group winners.
body: Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists, with Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also on the scoresheet as the hosts delivered their most impressive display so far under Jürgen Klopp’s leadership.

It was Germany’s biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959, and the Netherlands’ first defeat since Xavi Hernández took over as coach in August. The Dutch have still advanced to the last eight by finishing second, with Germany’s fifth goal taking Klopp’s side into top spot.

The visitors had the first good chance when Jurriën Timber found Crysencio Summerville unmarked on the penalty spot, but the winger lost his footing before getting a shot away. Germany then went close as the Berlin native Scherhant hit a post after connecting with a cross from his Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu.

Nine minutes later, Scherhant had another chance from the same spot and this time curled a lovely effort across the face of goal and inside the far post. Germany pushed for more goals after the break, and Wirtz delivered with a superb solo effort on the hour, lifting a shot in off the left post from the edge of the penalty area.

Dutch advance, Greece miss out despite win over Serbia.
Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany delivered a 5-0 rout of the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday, reaching the Nations League quarter-finals as group winners.

articles.title: Littler hits triple-bull, but Price checkout doesn't add up
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price and Luke Littler make it through to the Grand Slam of Darts knockout stage after a rare counting error and a sensational triple-bull checkout in Wolverhampton.
body: Gerwyn Price and Luke Littler both made it through to the Grand Slam of Darts knockout stage on a night featuring a bizarre maths error and a sensational triple-bull checkout.
Littler suffered a 5-4 defeat by Dutchman Niels Zonneveld but claimed the three legs he required to progress from the group stage.

The 19-year-old, egged on by the crowd at the Aldersley venue in Wolverhampton, improbably landed three darts on the bullseye to produce a remarkable 150 checkout and level the match at 4-4, only to lose the deciding leg.
Price, meanwhile, claimed a 5-2 victory over Sebastian Bialecki - although he was the beneficiary of an unusual mathematical mistake.

articles.title: Pocognoli wants patience but Scotland 'don't have time' says Robertson
articles.summary: Angry captain Andy Robertson says Scotland do not have time to turn things around after a brutal 4-0 defeat by Switzerland consigns them to a third-place finish in their Nations League group.
body: Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli - appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August - has consistently stressed the need for patience as he tries to implement a more attack-minded style.
However, the Belgian has won just two of his first six matches in charge, both against North Macedonia, and conceded 10 goals in that time.

They collapsed worryingly easily in St Gallen against a much-changed Swiss outfit on Monday after a promising start, Bologna midfielder Lewis Ferguson putting through his own goal and early intensity gave way to indecision.
The Swiss struck twice in the early minutes of the second half to make it 3-0 and Zeki Amdouni made it four late on.

articles.title: Robertson makes history with record 103rd Scotland cap
articles.summary: Andy Robertson has broken the record for the most senior Scotland men's team caps, surpassing the feat held by Sir Kenny Dalglish for 40 years.
body: Andy Robertson became Scotland's most-capped player with start against Switzerland in Nations League; he passed Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps; Robertson on Sir Kenny: "I don't want to forget and I don't want people to forget how important this man has been for our country."
The Scotland captain made his 103rd appearance for the national side in Monday's 4-0 defeat to Switzerland in the Nations League.
He has bypassed the record set by Dalglish, who earned 102 caps between 1971 and 1986.
Before hitting the milestone, Robertson insisted he will always regard Dalglish as "the greatest".

articles.title: 'I didn't know' - Price's controversial 145 checkout at Grand Slam explained
articles.summary: Gerwyn Price produced a controversial 145 checkout en route to a routine Grand Slam of Darts victory over Sebastian Bialecki on Monday night in Wolverhampton.
body: Price, the three-time champion in Wolverhampton, came through 5-2 against Poland's Bialecki to book his place in the knockout stage.
However, there was controversy during the final Group E match as Price hit a 145 finish when he had 135 remaining in the fourth leg of the match.
'The Iceman' needed 135 to hold his throw, and he thought he had taken it out.
After hitting T19 he asked referee Charlie Corstophine what he had left and was told 88.

articles.title: Wales have a free hit against Ronaldo-less Portugal
articles.summary: The Cardiff City Stadium sold out very quickly when the Nations League fixtures threw up a Wales vs Portugal game for the final match of Group D.
body: Mark the date, November 17, 2026 - it could have been the last time to see Cristiano Ronaldo play on UK soil.

A mouthwatering occasion to witness one of the greats of the game as the curtain slowly falls on his illustrious international career and also see just how far Wales are progressing after a full campaign in League A of the Nations League, a full campaign among the heavyweights of European football.

As we all know, that's not how it's panned out! After Ronaldo's appearance against Wales in Lisbon at the start of the Nations League, he's not featured since - and he's now called time on his Portugal career amid some controversy.

Even though Ronaldo's not here in Wales and the ending of his Portugal days were perhaps not the best scripted, he'll certainly be missed by many. Wales manager Craig Bellamy for one: "As soon as he retires then suddenly like, it's all hell breaks loose!

articles.title: Pistons lose two key players ahead of road game vs. Spurs
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO — The Detroit Pistons will be significantly short-handed against the 12-2 San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at Frost Bank Center. The Pistons announced in Monday's injury report that Ron Holland II and Duncan Robinson are out.
body: Holland will miss the game with a left knee contusion and a bone bruise he sustained late in the fourth quarter of Saturday's 137-117 loss to the Miami Heat. Holland's injury came after Robinson was ruled out after halftime with a left quadriceps strain.

Holland has had a slow start to his third season, averaging 4.9 points on 34.4% shooting. However, the former lottery pick (No. 5 overall in 2024) has found different ways to showcase his importance. In a game against the Heat, Holland had one of his most impactful performances, contributing beyond scoring. He grabbed five offensive rebounds, finished with seven boards, three assists and one steal against the Heat.

Against the Spurs, Robinson's absence will leave a bigger hole for the Pistons, since he has taken the helm as the team's second-best offensive player, averaging a career-best 17.4 points on a team-best 43.1% shooting from deep, along with 1.3 steals through the first 12 games.

body: Karl-Anthony Towns finished with 28 points, 17 rebounds and three assists in the team’s win against the Raptors, tying Bellamy for 13 double-doubles to start a season for the Knicks. Towns has continued to be a bright spot for the Knicks despite having his contract extension talks tabled by the organization for the time being.

The six-time All-Star is in his third full season with the Knicks after being acquired via trade with the Minnesota Timberwolves prior to the start of the 2024-25 season. He was instrumental in the Knicks’ title run last year, securing the franchise’s first championship in over 50 years.

This season, Towns has appeared in 13 games for the Knicks at a little over 32 minutes per game. He’s been averaging 21.6 points, a league-leading 13.9 rebounds and 3.6 assists with splits of 53.4 percent shooting from the field, 39.7 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 76.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Towns is also leading the league in defensive rebounds at 10.8.

articles.title: Klopp's Germany Routs Xavi's Netherlands To Book Nations League Quarterfinals
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz scored twice and Germany booked its place in the Nations League quarterfinals by routing the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin on Monday. More importantly, it was confirmation of the German team’s renaissance under new coach Jürgen Klopp, whose appointment ushered in new optimism around his…
body: Nico Schlotterbeck was the oldest goalscorer at 26, Wirtz is still just 23, the 24-year-old Derry Scherhant broke the deadlock, and Brajan Gruda, 22, set up two goals and scored one on what was just his second appearance for Germany. He also scored on his debut in Friday’s 3-1 win in Serbia.

It was the most emphatic win for Germany under Klopp, and the worst loss so far for Netherlands manager Xavi Hernandez. The World Cup-winning Spanish midfielder and club legend at Barcelona took over the Dutch job in August.
Klopp clearly enjoyed each of the goals, but he praised the players' work rate as key.

"Everyone who was here today is going home with a smile, and won’t be questioning the German national team for the next three or four months. That’s a good thing," Klopp said, referring to the previous negativity around the side. "When you think of the German team, this could develop into something, and that’s good."
